title: Surat Thani 2-Day Cafe & City Plan — Tapi River, Markets
metaDesc: A 2-day cafe-hopping plan for Surat Thani town, Thailand: real roasteries in Ban Don, a walk along the Tapi River, Lamphu Island, the city pillar shrine, and the Narit Bridge walking street — timed for when places actually open.

ogTitle: Surat Thani 2-Day Cafe + City Plan — Tapi River, Markets, Cafes
ogDesc: Take Surat Thani town slowly: sip local coffee, stroll the Tapi River, hit the markets — with timings that match when places really open.
intro: Plenty of people pass through Surat Thani only to catch a ferry out to the islands, never realizing that Ban Don town itself is more fun than they'd guess. The old quarter along the Tapi River is full of new cafes roasting their own beans, plus a morning market, an evening market, a riverside walking street, and a green island park you can stroll all day. This is a 2-day plan for anyone who wants to take the town slowly — sitting with coffee, wandering around, and eating well — timed to match when places actually open.

blocks.html: Surat Thani town (locals call it Ban Don) sits along the Tapi River just before it opens into Ban Don Bay. It's an old trading port that still has its rows of old shophouses, Chinese shrines, and a fresh market that buzzes every morning. You can do almost all of this plan within a radius of a few kilometers — songthaews (red trucks), motorbike taxis, or a rented motorbike all make it easy. It's a good fit for anyone arriving before or after an island trip who wants to give the town a proper 2 days.

blocks.title: Before you set out
blocks.html: Many cafes in town close on a weekday mid-week (Tuesday or Wednesday are the common ones), the Narit Bridge walking street runs only on Saturdays, and the Ban Don floating market is a Sunday evening thing. If you want to catch both the cafes and the riverside markets, planning a trip across Saturday–Sunday works out best.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Old-Town Cafes + Evening on the Tapi

blocks.html: Day one is about getting to know the town. Start with a southern-style breakfast, then work your way through the house-roasting cafes around the old market quarter, before finishing the day with the riverside atmosphere along the Tapi at sunset.

items.activity: Surat-style breakfast in Ban Don fresh market
items.note: The town's fresh market has old-school coffee, pa thong ko (fried dough), dim sum, and rice porridge, starting around ฿30–60 a plate — a breakfast locals actually eat.

items.activity: First cup at Rocket Coffee Roastery & Baking
items.note: On Talat Mai Road, a loft-style spot that roasts its own. The signature drinks are orange coffee and matcha, with bakery to pair. Coffee around ฿65–95.

items.activity: Walk the old buildings and Chinese shrines in the market quarter
items.note: Ban Don still has wooden shophouses and old shrines — easy, pleasant photo stops on the way to the next cafe.

items.activity: Tucked-away second cafe — Doz Coffee Lab
items.note: Near the central intersection, roasting its beans in-house. A specialty crowd-pleaser (closed Wednesdays), open roughly 09:00–16:00.

items.activity: Lunch — khanom jeen or punchy southern food
items.note: Pick a southern restaurant in town and order gaeng tai pla, stir-fried stink beans, and khua kling, eaten with fresh raw veg on the side. A genuinely filling meal for ฿80–150.

items.activity: Afternoon break at Backyard Cafe X TCT
items.note: A cafe in a lane near the river, with ice cream and sweets, plus a cute cactus corner for photos. Open until about 18:30.

items.activity: Evening stroll along the Tapi River
items.note: The riverside walkway in town catches a cool breeze, with views of fishing boats and the bridges across the river. It's a free sunset spot where locals come to walk.

items.activity: Riverside dinner at Brown Sugar Cafe & Bistro
items.note: A spot right on the Tapi River with Thai food, coffee, cakes, and drinks. You can linger late (open until midnight).

blocks.title: About closing days
blocks.html: Rocket, Doz, and several other cafes in town take their weekly day off on different days. A quick check of each shop's page before you leave your hotel saves a wasted trip. If one is closed, the same area still has Square Coffee, Tree Space, and Kafae Ban Pu to swap in.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Lamphu Island · City Pillar Shrine · Walking Street

blocks.html: Day two starts at the river-island park in the morning for the good air, with a stop to pay respects at the Srivijaya-style city pillar shrine, picks up any cafes you haven't reached, and wraps up at the riverside walking street in the evening (plan it for a Saturday to get the full set).

items.note: An island in the middle of the Tapi River — the town's green lung. Free entry, open from before dawn until 22:00, with walking and cycling paths along the water. Mornings are cool and quiet.

items.activity: Morning coffee at Good Cafe' (below Blu Monkey Hotel)
items.note: Opens early at 07:00, with plenty of bakery and donuts — a good stop after the park walk. Coffee around ฿60–90.

items.activity: Pay respects at the Surat Thani city pillar shrine
items.note: Near the Ban Don market by the Tapi River, with Srivijaya-style architecture rooted in local culture. Free to visit.

items.activity: Lunch — oysters or Ban Don Bay seafood
items.note: Surat Thani is known for the plump oysters from Ban Don Bay. Try fresh oysters or a stir-fried seafood dish at a restaurant in town.
A house-roasting spot down a lane, with sparkling coffee and pumpkin coffee as standouts. Quiet and good for working. Open roughly 09:00–18:00.

items.activity: Start the Narit Bridge walking street (Saturdays only)
items.note: Along the Tapi River by Narit Bridge, open 16:00–22:00 every Saturday. Loads of food — fried, grilled, sweets — plus OTOP souvenirs.

items.activity: Dinner at the riverside market, then a long walk along the Tapi
items.note: Graze your way down the stalls; there's riverside seating in the breeze. An easy way to close out the city trip.

blocks.title: If you're not here on a Saturday
blocks.html: The Narit Bridge walking street is Saturdays only, and the Ban Don floating market is Sunday evenings. If your trip lands on a weekday, switch dinner to the riverside at Brown Sugar, or walk the shrine market / the 100-year-old Saphan Khong (Arched Bridge) market, which opens in the evening instead.

blocks.text: Cafes Worth a Stop in Town (Ordered by Buzz)

blocks.html: The plan above slots in cafes to match your walking pace, but Surat Thani town has plenty more house-roasting spots than that. Here are the ones locals and reviews mention most often, in case you want to swap based on closing days or your own taste.

items.name: Rocket Coffee Roastery & Baking
items.blurb: A house-roasting favorite with the town's younger crowd, semi-minimal loft style. Signature drinks are orange coffee and matcha, with bakery and truffle pizza too.
items.meta: Talat Mai / old-market area · open roughly 08:00–17:00

items.name: Doz Coffee Lab
items.blurb: Specialty leaning, roasting its own beans in-house, with a compact setting near the central intersection. Coffee people like it (closed Wednesdays).

items.name: Sipster Roaster
items.blurb: Down a deep lane, calm and quiet. Standout drinks are sparkling coffee and pumpkin coffee, with cake to pair — good for working.

items.name: Tree Space Cafe
items.blurb: A pour-over and specialty cafe in the Si Ket area, with croissants and signature drinks in an airy space (closed Wednesdays).

items.name: Square Coffee and Space
items.blurb: Opens early at seven, ideal for early risers. Matcha and signature coffee drinks, with cakes to choose from.

items.name: Good Cafe' Surat Thani
items.blurb: Below the Blu Monkey Hotel, opens early with plenty of bakery and donuts — a good stop before or after the Lamphu Island park walk.

items.name: Backyard Cafe X TCT
items.blurb: A cafe in a lane near the river, with ice cream, prettily plated sweets, and a cactus corner for photos. Afternoons draw a chilled crowd.
items.meta: Lane near the river · until about 18:30

items.name: Brown Sugar Cafe & Bistro
items.blurb: Right on the Tapi River, both cafe and bistro, with Thai food, coffee, cake, and alcoholic drinks. You can settle in late into the night.

items.name: Le Viridian HoTown & Cafe
items.blurb: A central-town cafe leaning European bakery, with house-made drinks and baked goods (closed Tuesdays).

items.name: Kafae Ban Pu
items.blurb: A white-toned minimalist spot in town, open daily, with plenty of bakery — an easy drop-in with no closing-day gamble.

blocks.title: Cafe-hopper tips
blocks.html: House-roasting cafes in a small town often have limited tables, and weekend afternoons get crowded. If you want a good seat, go before 1 pm — and don't set out to hit every shop. Picking about 2 cafes a day and settling in properly is more fun.

blocks.text: Markets and Riverside Spots Not to Miss

items: Narit Bridge walking street (Saturdays 16:00–22:00) — along the Tapi River, with loads of food (fried, grilled, sweets) and OTOP souvenirs. It's the town's evening-market highlight.
Ban Don floating market (Sunday evenings) — a worth-seeing market on the Tapi River near the city pillar shrine, with a riverside atmosphere and local eats.
Lamphu Island public park — an island in the middle of the Tapi River, free entry, open 04:00–22:00, with walking and cycling paths along the water. Mornings and evenings have the best air.
Ban Don fresh market — a morning market in the heart of town with old-school coffee, dim sum, pa thong ko, and fresh seafood. It's where locals eat breakfast.
City pillar shrine + old market quarter — Srivijaya-style art near the river, with old shophouses and Chinese shrines to walk on to.

blocks.text: Getting Around Town and Where to Stay

blocks.html: Ban Don town is small and walkable — most spots in this plan are within a radius of a few kilometers. Songthaews (red trucks) run around town, and motorbike taxis are easy to flag. If you want more freedom, renting a motorbike by the day is the easiest option. For where to stay, pick an area near the Ban Don market or the Tapi riverfront so you can easily walk into the cafes and markets. Surat Thani Airport is about 25 km outside town, roughly a 30–40 minute drive in.

faq.q: How many days do you need for cafe-hopping in Surat Thani town?
faq.a: Two days is about right. Day one works through the old-town cafes and the Tapi riverfront in the evening; day two covers Lamphu Island park, the city pillar shrine, and the walking street. If you only have one day, pick 2 cafes plus the riverside in the evening.

faq.q: Are cafes in Surat Thani town open every day?
faq.a: Not all of them. Many house-roasting cafes take a weekly day off — Tuesday or Wednesday are common. Doz Coffee and Tree Space, for example, close on Wednesdays, while Kafae Ban Pu is open daily. It's worth checking each shop's page before you go.

faq.q: Which days is the Tapi River walking street on?
faq.a: The Narit Bridge walking street runs every Saturday, 16:00–22:00, along the Tapi River by Narit Bridge. The Ban Don floating market is a Sunday evening thing. If you want both, plan a trip across Saturday–Sunday.

faq.q: Is Lamphu Island public park free, and what are its hours?
faq.a: It's free, open from before dawn around 04:00 until 22:00. It's an island in the middle of the Tapi River where you can stroll and cycle along the water. Mornings are cool and quiet.

faq.q: What's the easiest way to get around Surat Thani town?
faq.a: Ban Don town is small and walkable in many places, with songthaews (red trucks) running around town and motorbike taxis available. If you want more freedom, renting a motorbike by the day is the easiest option. The airport is about 25 km outside town.
